items.title: Maternal Inner Strength Mediates the Longitudinal Association Between Family Emotional Expression and Fear of Childbirth: A Cross-Lagged Panel Mediation Analysis.
items.authors: Ma D, Sun Y, Wang XY, Cao D.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Fear of childbirth (FOC) increases maternal and perinatal adverse health risks, and family factors are core predictors of FOC. This study aimed to clarify the mediating pathway through which familial emotional expression (FEE) is associated with FOC via pregnant women's inner strength (IS), so as to supply empirical basis for antenatal psychological risk management.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A longitudinal survey was performed among pregnant women from the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of a tertiary Grade A hospital in Shenyang from September 2023 to August 2024. A total of 136 participants completed questionnaires in early, middle and late pregnancy, including the Childbirth Attitude Questionnaire (CAQ), Family Environment Scale (FES) and Inner Strength Scale (ISS). Two sets of longitudinal analyses were performed on this sample: latent class growth modeling (LCGM) was conducted via Mplus 8.3 to identify heterogeneous developmental trajectories of FOC; separately, cross-lagged panel mediation analyses were carried out with SPSS 26 and Amos 26.0 using the full-sample raw longitudinal data to examine the mediating mechanism among FEE, IS, and FOC.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Three distinct FOC developmental trajectories were identified: "Low FOC stable group" (11.4%), "Moderate FOC stable group" (33.5%), and "High FOC elevated group" (55.1%). FEE was longitudinally associated with IS (β=0.691, P<0.001), while IS was longitudinally associated with FOC in a negative direction (β=-0.552, P<0.001). No significant association was observed between FEE and FOC (β=0.079, P=0.293). The total effect of FEE on FOC was -0.303 (P<0.05), the direct effect was 0.079 (P>0.05), and the indirect effect was -0.382 (P<0.05), proving that the effect of FEE on FOC operates through IS.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: FOC presents heterogeneous developmental trajectories across different gestational trimesters. FEE is indirectly associated with lower FOC levels by promoting pregnant women's IS. The findings provide empirical evidence for understanding the developmental characteristics and psychological influencing factors of FOC, and can inform targeted, individualized antenatal psychological screening and intervention strategies to alleviate childbirth fear and improve maternal mental health in clinical obstetric care.

items.title: Understanding stress through metabolomic and psychosocial lenses: Pathways to biomarker discovery.
items.authors: Atrooz F, Zenati RA, Semreen MH, Alzoubi KH, Al-Hroub HM, Bustanji Y, Khabour OF, Aljararwah S, Salim S.

sections.text: Identifying reliable biomarkers of trauma-related psychological stress is critical for accurate diagnosis and appropriate intervention. Metabolomic profiling offers a promising approach to uncover biochemical correlates of stress. This study investigated salivary metabolomic signatures of traumatic stress in Syrian refugee women resettled in Jordan, with Jordanian women serving as a comparison group. We conducted a cross-sectional study to assess mental distress among Syrian refugee (n = 48) and Jordanian women (n = 52) living in northern Jordan. Saliva samples were collected and processed from all participants, of which 25 (11 Syrian refugee and 14 Jordanian women) yielded sufficiently detectable metabolomic profiles and were included in the exploratory metabolomic analysis. Psychometric assessments included validated measures of perceived stress and mental distress. Saliva samples were analyzed using global quantitative metabolomics via high-resolution TIMS-TOF mass spectrometry to identify metabolites associated with stress. While Syrian refugee women reported higher perceived stress compared with Jordanian women (mean ± SD: 30.72 ± 9.2 vs. 27.19 ± 7.7; p = 0.040), both Jordanian and Syrian women exhibited high scores in Self Reporting Questionnaire (mean score ± SD: Syrian refugees = 11.59 ± 4.5, Jordanian women = 10.60 ± 4.7; p = 0.285). Syrian refugee women exhibited elevated salivary metabolites linked to oxido-inflammatory and stress-response pathways including purine metabolism, glutathione metabolism, pyrimidine metabolism, and plasmalogen synthesis. Our findings point to salivary metabolites involved in oxido-inflammatory cascades as potential biomarkers of psychological stress, which in the future may provide objective, noninvasive indicators of stress, complementing psychometric assessments and offering new avenues for evaluating mental health risk in vulnerable populations such as refugees. Findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of causality.

items.title: Inflammatory Bowel Disease, Self-Esteem and Sexual Well-Being.
items.authors: O'Reilly K, Holroyd E, You W, Peters K.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: This research explored associations between self-esteem, satisfaction with physical appearance, sexual satisfaction and physical and mental health among women living with inflammatory bowel disease in Australia.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Inflammatory bowel disease which includes Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis is a chronic autoimmune disease. Its relapsing, remitting nature has deleterious impacts on self-esteem and sexual well-being.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study employed a cross-sectional design with secondary exploratory analyses and used an online survey to collect data from Australian women between March and November 2024.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Responses from 64 women revealed a nuanced but complex interrelationship between self-esteem and biopsychosocial factors which impact on sexual well-being. Self-esteem scores for all women sat at the low end of normal, and none of the women reported any level higher than average. Women with lower self-esteem reported more dissatisfaction with their physical appearance, poorer mental health and lower sexual satisfaction.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Having a high self-esteem is a protective factor in adaptation to life events. The chronic nature of inflammatory bowel disease highlights that adaptation and self-realignment are ongoing processes of which clinicians must be cognisant because chronic illness can have negative effects on self-esteem.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Sexual well-being is influenced by multiple intersecting biopsychosocial factors. Routinely incorporating discussions which relate to mental health, self-esteem and body image into assessments for people living with inflammatory bowel disease is critical in holistic care.

sections.heading: Implications for nursing
sections.text: The findings provide justification for integrated teams of psychologists, sexual health nurses and potentially body-image specialists which could be coordinated by registered nurses.

sections.heading: Implications for health policy
sections.text: Women-specific care pathways which acknowledge reproductive life stages, relationship health, sexual well-being, hormonal variation, menstrual impacts and sociocultural gender pressures are required. Introducing regular screening, which includes adding registries on digital platforms, may assist with ensuring equitable holistic healthcare.

items.title: Workload, Harassment, and Workplace Consultation Availability and Their Associations with Mental Distress among Physical Therapists.
items.authors: Kota M, Uezono S, Nishigori T, Chiba T, Nawai K.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: Physical therapists (PTs) face various psychosocial risks that affect their mental health; however, profession-specific reports on organizational exposures remain limited. This study aimed to examine total overtime, workplace harassment, and workplace consultation availability and their associations with current mental distress among PTs in Japan.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A nationwide cross-sectional web survey of PTs, conducted from August 12 to September 20, 2025, was analyzed. The primary outcome was current mental distress (yes/no). The main exposures were total overtime in the past 3 months (per 10 h/3 months), workplace harassment (yes/no), and workplace consultation availability (yes/no). Separate multivariable logistic models were fit for each exposure with a common adjustment set (sex, age, tenure in current workplace [midpoint, years], employment status, hospital bed size, and number of PTs). Missing covariates were handled via multiple imputation (multiple imputation by chained equations, m = 15) with pooling by Rubin's rules.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of the 718 PTs surveyed, 312 (43.5%) were classified as distress present. Mean total overtime was 16.7 ± 15.0 h over 3 months and was higher in the distress-present group. Adjusted associations were total overtime adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 1.13 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.98-1.31) per additional 10 h, harassment aOR 2.29 (95% CI 1.67-3.14), and workplace consultation availability aOR 0.60 (95% CI 0.43-0.84).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Workplace harassment was associated with higher rates of mental distress, whereas workplace consultation availability was inversely associated. Total overtime showed a positive trend in the adjusted model. These findings point to organizational targets, including overtime management, harassment prevention, and accessible consultation routes.

items.title: Graph theory-based machine learning for automated fibromyalgia diagnosis using fMRI during an emotional task.
items.authors: Solouki L, Shahsavari S, Sharini H, Hashemian AH, Johann Schmid V, Jafari S, Rouhi S, Mahaki B.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a multifaceted chronic pain disorder presenting with pain throughout the musculoskeletal system, alongside chronic fatigue,sleep disturbances, and cognitive impairments. Current diagnostic criteria primarily rely on symptom questionnaires, with no specific laboratory markers or definitive tests, making diagnosis subjective and often delayed. Moreover, the overlap with other central pain syndromes further complicates accurate diagnosis. Neuroimaging studies, particularly functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), have shown promise in elucidating brain abnormalities underlying FM. However, translating these findings into reliable diagnostic tools remains challenging, especially given small sample sizes. Therefore, this study aims to enhance the diagnostic accuracy of FM based on fMRI data by developing an intelligent model. This model employs machine learning algorithms designed to perform effectively with limited dataset sizes and incorporates features extracted through graph theory methods. We analyzed fMRI data from 32 FM patients and 30 healthy controls. Graph theory metrics were extracted from 13 regions of the emotion regulation network. A genetic algorithm was employed to select the most effective features, which were then used to train multiple machine learning classifiers-including Support Vector Machine (SVM) with polynomial and Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Machine, Adaptive Boosting, and SVM with Mixture Kernels-within a cross-validation framework to ensure robustness.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: The genetic algorithm selected 84 features as inputs for machine learning algorithms. The polynomial SVM achieved the highest overall accuracy, whereas the SVM with mixture kernels demonstrated superior sensitivity and AUC. Sensitivity and AUC were prioritized as the main criteria for model selection due to their clinical relevance in reducing false negatives.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The study identified the SVM with Mixture Kernels as the most effective model for distinguishing FM patients from healthy controls. This approach demonstrates promising potential for enhancing diagnostic accuracy and supporting psychological and psychiatric interventions.

items.title: The association between physical activity and perceived stress among adolescents: the serial mediating roles of social-emotional competence and prosocial behavior.
items.authors: Qu J, Shang C, Ding X, Liu S, Shi C, Chen B, Zhu Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adolescence is a critical developmental period characterized by heightened vulnerability to stress. Stressors such as academic demands, interpersonal relationships, and the family environment may intensify perceived stress (PS). Physical activity (PA) has been associated with adolescents' appraisal of and coping with stressful events, potentially in relation to psychosocial resources. This study examined the association between PA and PS and investigated the potential roles of social-emotional competence (SEC) and prosocial behavior (PB).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: PA, SEC, PB, and PS were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale-3 (PARS-3), the Social-Emotional Competence Questionnaire, the Prosocial Tendencies Measure, and the 14-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14), respectively. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical multiple regression analysis were conducted using SPSS 27.0. PROCESS 4.1 Model 6 was used to test the independent and serial mediating effects of SEC and PB.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: (1) PA was significantly negatively associated with PS ( β = -0.398, p  < 0.001). This association remained significant after SEC and PB were included ( β = -0.216, p  < 0.001). (2) The indirect association between PA and PS involving SEC was statistically significant ( b = -0.025, 95% CI [-0.030, -0.020]). (3) The indirect association between PA and PS involving PB was statistically significant ( b = -0.016, 95% CI [-0.020, -0.013]). (4) The serial indirect association between PA and PS involving SEC and PB was statistically significant ( b = -0.009, 95% CI [-0.011, -0.007]).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: PA was associated with lower PS among adolescents, and the indirect associations were consistent with the prespecified ordering of SEC and PB. These findings may inform future research on how team sports and sport-based public-service activities relate to adolescents' developmental resources, coping, and PS.

items.title: "You are not allowed to break down": psychological safety and the hidden curriculum of psychiatry training in China.
items.authors: Zhou C, Xie X, Zhang A, Li S.

sections.text: Mental health among medical trainees has typically been framed as an individual deficit, addressed through resilience training and counseling services. This perspective examines how the hidden curriculum within Chinese psychiatry training may shape psychological safety and professional identity formation. Drawing on psychological safety theory, hidden curriculum scholarship, Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems theory, and recent empirical literature on medical trainee distress in China, we propose a theoretically derived and empirically testable conceptual model through which experiences of vulnerability may become socially and professionally invisible. The proposed vulnerability-to-invisibility process describes four interconnected phases: the encounter with vulnerability, perceived or enacted prohibition of emotional expression, internalization of silence, and potential fragmentation of professional identity. Existing evidence supports several constituent components of this pathway, but direct empirical evidence establishing the complete sequence remains limited. We therefore call for institutional reforms that embed psychological safety into clinical training, including protected reflective spaces, reflective faculty modeling, peer support, and curriculum-integrated mentorship, while emphasizing adaptive emotional regulation rather than forced suppression.

items.title: Adaptation and psychometric evaluation of the Natural Disasters Picture System (NDPS) to the Spanish population.
items.authors: Mendoza DA, Reales JM, Ballesteros S.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Climate change is causing an increase in natural disasters and extreme weather events. This threat is impacting the mental health of those who experience it. However, empirical research in the Spanish context is limited by the lack of culturally adapted tools.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this study, we have adapted and validated with a Spanish sample composed by 73 participants the Natural Disasters Picture System (NDPS). The methodology incorporated Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), Mixed Linear Models (MLM) with intercepts for subjects and stimuli, and predictive classification using Machine Learning (Random Forest).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The results demonstrated the cross-cultural robustness of the original four clusters ("Frightening," "Desolation," "Neutral" and "Pleasant/Aesthetic"). Additionally, we identified a unidimensional latent factor and a significant perceptual overlap between "Frightening" (fear) and "Desolation" (sadness) in the Machine Learning Model.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: The NDPS provides a set of visual stimuli that can be used to investigate risk perception and the elicitation of emotions. Despite the appropriate distribution of commonalities and the accuracy of MLMs, that support the instrument's properties, we acknowledge the possible limitation sample.

items.title: Beyond cultural competence: a qualitative analysis of psychologists' experiences with Muslim clients in South Africa.
items.authors: Salie M, Kagee A.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Muslim mental health is an emerging field of inquiry in the global South. Understanding how mental health conditions are interpreted within diverse Muslim communities is important for culturally responsive psychological care.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This qualitative study explored psychologists' experiences of providing services to Muslim clients in the Western Cape, South Africa, and explored psychologists' accounts of explanatory models of mental health conditions encountered in therapeutic practice. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 clinical and counseling psychologists practicing in the Western Cape. Data were analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Three themes were constructed. First, psychologists emphasized the importance of understanding Muslim clients within their broader sociocultural and historical context, particularly the enduring influence of Apartheid, migration histories, intergenerational trauma, and institutional mistrust. Second, psychologists reported encountering diverse explanatory models among Muslim clients, including interpretations of distress in relation to religiosity, supernatural influences, stigma, personal weakness, and biomedical understandings. These explanatory models were described as shaping emotions such as fear, guilt, and shame, as well as pathways to help-seeking and engagement with treatment. Third, psychologists highlighted the importance of culturally responsive practice, including reflexive engagement with clients' religious worldviews, ongoing self-education, culturally informed supervision, and ethical collaboration with Muslim religious leaders.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: The findings suggest that explanatory models are not solely individual beliefs about MHC but are embedded within broader religious, familial, historical, and sociopolitical contexts. By exploring psychologists' accounts of therapeutic encounters with Muslim clients in the Western Cape, this study extends explanatory-model scholarship by highlighting how collective histories and relationships with systems of care shape understandings of mental health and help-seeking.

items.title: Exercise adherence and subjective well-being: the chain mediating roles of self-efficacy and outcome expectations.
items.authors: Liang J, Zhao J.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: Although the rising prevalence of mental health issues among Chinese university students is influenced by multiple factors, it has been significantly associated with a lack of regular physical activity. The present study aims to examine the relationship between exercise adherence and subjective wellbeing among university students, specifically testing the mediating effects of self-efficacy and outcome expectations within a chain mediation framework.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A questionnaire-based survey was conducted among a sample of 435 undergraduate students at Shandong Normal University (50.57% male, 49.43% female). The study employed validated instruments, including the Exercise Adherence Scale, the Self-Efficacy Scale, the Outcome Expectations Scale, and the Subjective Wellbeing Scale. Correlation and regression analyses, integrated with chain mediation modeling, were employed to examine the associations between exercise adherence, self-efficacy, outcome expectations, and subjective wellbeing.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Exercise adherence was significantly associated with subjective wellbeing both directly (effect value = 0.043) and indirectly through self-efficacy (effect value = 0.036), outcome expectations (effect value = 0.023), and the chain mediation of self-efficacy and outcome expectations (effect value = 0.012). Regression analysis revealed that exercise adherence significantly and positively predicted subjective wellbeing (β = 0.397, p < 0.001). After accounting for the indirect associations via self-efficacy and outcome expectations, exercise adherence remained significantly and positively associated with subjective wellbeing (β = 0.150, p = 0.002).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Exercise adherence among Chinese university students is significantly and positively correlated with subjective wellbeing. This relationship is further linked to the chain mediating roles of self-efficacy and outcome expectations. Specifically, higher levels of exercise adherence are associated with greater self-efficacy, which relates to more positive outcome expectations, and both factors subsequently correlate with higher subjective wellbeing. Consequently, interventions focusing on these psychological variables may be beneficial in supporting the overall physical and mental health of university students.

items.title: High awareness but low utilization: How perceived institutional support shapes college students' mental health through stigma?
items.authors: Luo D, Gu X, Wang H, Zhang L.

sections.text: In the context of high awareness but low utilization of university counseling services, an important question is whether university mental health support may still carry psychological significance when actual service use remains limited. Drawing on social support theory and stigma theory, this study extends the understanding of university mental health support beyond a utilization-based perspective by examining whether students' perceptions of university mental health support are associated with mental health through perceived stigma. Using survey data from 642 university students in China, this study developed an analytical model examining the associations among perceived institutional support, perceived stigma, and mental health outcomes. The results showed that perceived institutional support was positively associated with mental health and negatively associated with perceived stigma. In addition, perceived stigma was negatively associated with mental health and statistically accounted for part of the observed association between perceived institutional support and mental health, suggesting an indirect association consistent with the proposed theoretical model. These findings suggest that the potential value of university mental health support may extend beyond actual counseling utilization. Rather, students' perceptions of institutional recognition, accessibility, and acceptance of psychological support may represent an important aspect of the campus mental health environment. This perspective is particularly relevant within the Chinese higher education context, where concerns about social evaluation and stigma may influence students' willingness to acknowledge psychological difficulties and seek support. This study contributes to the literature by moving beyond a utilization-based framework and highlighting the potential contextual significance of perceived institutional support in relation to stigma and mental health. Practically, the findings suggest that Chinese universities may consider not only service availability but also students' perceptions of institutional support when evaluating campus mental health environments.

items.title: A qualitative study on the delayed manifestation of night shift-related intrusive memories in non-shift nurses with a history of night shift work.
items.authors: Gai X, Hao Z, Jiang C, Liu M, Yang Q, Xu H.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The adverse effects of night shift work on the physical and mental health of nurses have been widely documented. However, little is known about whether these psychological experiences persist after nurses cease working night shifts or whether some of these experiences subsequently manifest as intrusive memories.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To explore the characteristics of the delayed manifestation of night shift-related intrusive memories and the associated experiences among non-shift nurses with a history of night shift work.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A descriptive qualitative study design was employed using a descriptive phenomenological approach. Fifteen non-shift nurses with a history of night shift work who were currently working fixed day shifts at a Grade III Class A hospital in Shandong Province were recruited for semi-structured interviews. Colaizzi's seven-step method was used for data analysis. The findings were reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guideline.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among nurses who reported night shift-related intrusive experiences after the cessation of night shift duties, these experiences may persist for months or even years and may be reactivated by specific situational cues, accompanied by emotional responses. Four themes were identified: Night Shift-Related Psychosocial Stressors; Characteristics of Night Shift-Related Intrusive Memories; Contextual Cues and Persistent Experiences Following Night Shift Work; and Coping and Meaning Reconstruction After Night Shift Experiences.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Among nurses who reported night shift-related intrusive experiences after the cessation of night shift duties, these experiences were characterized by delayed onset, involuntary recurrence, and situational dependence. These findings highlight the importance of recognizing the psychological experiences of nurses with a history of night shift work and suggest the need for appropriate occupational mental health support and adaptation strategies.
